subject: Physics
required_symbol_fields_reason: A Physics symbol is meaningless without its unit and dimensions; dimensional consistency is a check the subject can actually run.

validator_catalogue.proves: The stated magnitude follows from the two declared perpendicular components.
validator_catalogue.does_not_prove: That the components themselves were derived correctly, or that the frame was chosen correctly.

validator_catalogue.proves: The final velocity follows from the declared initial velocity, acceleration and elapsed time.
validator_catalogue.does_not_prove: That constant acceleration is the right model for the situation.

validator_catalogue.proves: The initial velocity follows by inversion of the constant-acceleration relation.
validator_catalogue.does_not_prove: That constant acceleration is the right model for the situation.

validator_catalogue.proves: The elapsed time to reach the stated velocity under the declared acceleration.
validator_catalogue.does_not_prove: That the event occurs within the physical situation's validity window.

validator_catalogue.proves: The apex time and state under a no-drag constant-g model.
validator_catalogue.does_not_prove: That drag is negligible in the described situation.

validator_catalogue.proves: Average speed from total distance and average velocity from signed displacement over the same positive interval.
validator_catalogue.does_not_prove: That listed leg speeds may be averaged arithmetically or that the interval is appropriate for an instantaneous velocity.

validator_catalogue.proves: The gravitational-force magnitude follows from the declared masses, gravitational constant and centre-to-centre separation.
validator_catalogue.does_not_prove: That point-mass or spherically symmetric modelling is appropriate for the described bodies.

requires: r is measured from the source centre
validator_catalogue.proves: The gravitational acceleration magnitude produced by the declared source mass at the declared radius.
validator_catalogue.does_not_prove: That other gravitational sources or non-gravitational forces are negligible.

requires: rho is constant over the compared depth interval
validator_catalogue.proves: The static-pressure difference follows from density, gravitational acceleration and signed depth change.
validator_catalogue.does_not_prove: That the fluid is static or incompressible enough for constant density to be appropriate.

validator_catalogue.proves: The internal-energy change follows from Q - W under the declared work-by-system-positive convention.
validator_catalogue.does_not_prove: That the chosen system boundary or measured heat/work transfers are physically appropriate.

validator_catalogue.proves: Wave speed follows from frequency times wavelength for the declared travelling-wave description.
validator_catalogue.does_not_prove: That the medium is nondispersive or that the same speed applies after the medium changes.

validator_catalogue.proves: Average power follows from net work transferred over the declared positive time interval.
validator_catalogue.does_not_prove: That power was constant during the interval.

requires: force_parallel is the signed component of force along the instantaneous velocity direction
validator_catalogue.proves: Instantaneous power follows from the signed along-velocity force component times instantaneous speed.
validator_catalogue.does_not_prove: That the supplied force component or velocity is correctly resolved from the physical situation.

requires: voltage and current use one consistent passive/sign convention for the element
validator_catalogue.proves: Electrical power follows from the declared element voltage and current under the stated sign convention.
validator_catalogue.does_not_prove: That an Ohmic V-I model applies or that the element is dissipative.

requires: resultant labelled with tail and head
one length scale for every vector drawn
limits: a construction, not a component readout; VECTOR draws one vector against axes, and using it here would hide the reversal that the construction exists to show

requires: explicit labelled y minimum when not zero
limits: piecewise-linear interpolation only; must not imply a curved model

changes_on_port: Promoted the six learner products to the primary structure; dropped the legacy four-Core runtime role block (no legacy runtime exists in this repository).
Moved result units and comparison semantics out of engine code (publication_host/science.py RESULT_UNITS) into validator_catalogue, so the shared engine carries no subject-specific units table.
Added explicit proves / does_not_prove per validator family.
Added curriculum binding authority with a fail-closed unbound state, adapted from PR #350's physics-curriculum-scope-bindings registry.
